claim.value: Reproducible differences under common conditions would support distinguishable onboarding behaviors.
claim.scope: Conditional support for behavioral distinctions, not an assertion that differences have been observed or causes identified.

provenance.rationale: P018 supplies the conditional behavioral inference and its reproducibility and common-condition requirements. P027 supplies the boundary against identifying causes from behavioral retention alone.

signal_basis.value: Reproducible concentrations of trajectories differ in milestone position, waiting duration, returns to active work or time to first publication under common onboarding and observation conditions.
signal_basis.scope: Prospective cohort comparisons using the same onboarding pathway and comparable observation windows, accounting for conditions that can shift apparent retention.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the trajectory measurements, reproducibility requirement, common pathway and observation conditions, and qualifications concerning factors that shift retention. P001 identifies the prospective cohort.
No additional unresolved empirical relation is needed for this bounded descriptive inference.

rationale: Reproducible differences in measured onboarding trajectories under comparable conditions support distinguishing observed behaviors. The claim does not require those differences to establish fixed customer segments or identify underlying causes.
uncertainty: The signal leaves causal explanations unresolved, but that uncertainty does not defeat the claimed behavioral distinction.
